Crypto’s quantum future deserves more than a fear narrative.

The real question is who moves the funds and who pays.
The panel at Quantum + Privacy Day was not a demo of a new chain. It was a recap of the product vision: privacy by default on the chains people already use, with quantum resistance as the long-term ambition, not a current toggle.

@Americanfort_io’s approach is ZKPoSP. Same address format. Same seed behind it. Funds do not move. The signature step is replaced by a zero-knowledge proof that the signer controls the full BIP32 derivation chain. ~6.65 seconds to generate the proof, ~475 ms to verify.

The bridge angle they showed is the same idea applied to payouts: prove ownership without handing over a name or a history. No proof, no payout. Same-owner verification across chains. Existing address. No migration weekend for normal users.

Send-to-Name™ is the part that is already live. You pay @‌name. The wallet computes a fresh address for that payment. Only the sender and the recipient can derive it. Settlement stays on the chain you were already using. The name does not publish a permanent wallet.

I care more about the migration problem than the curve. If the answer is “move your funds,” most people will not. The live product is the name and the one-time address. Quantum resistance is the future layer on top of that.

Would you migrate a wallet for a future threat, or only if the address you already use could be protected without a move?
